items.title: The one-centre Coulomb model: position and radial distributions of the bound states, with the ground-state density and its scales
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the framework postulates P1, P2 and P5, the readings of the declared
one-centre Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with
parameters $\hbar>0$, $m>0$, $\kappa>0$ and length scale
$a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, the energy-observable reading of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]], the bound-state data
of [[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]], and the
spin-zero position law
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For each label let $\psi_{nlm}$ and
$\Psi_{nlm}=\psi_{nlm}/\|\psi_{nlm}\|$ be the bound vectors of the cited
theorem, and write $u_{nl}$ for the reduced regular solution with
$\psi_{nlm}(x)=u_{nl}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$. Then:

(a) for every label and every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$ the position
outcome law in the unit preparation $[\Psi_{nlm}]$ is
$$\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{nlm}}(B)=\|\psi_{nlm}\|^{-2}\int_{0}^{\infty}|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}\Bigl(\int_{S^{2}}\mathbf 1_{B}(r\Omega)\,|Y_{lm}(\Omega)|^{2}\,d\sigma(\Omega)\Bigr)dr;$$
in particular, for a **radial** set $B=\{x:a<|x|<b\}$ with
$0\le a<b\le+\infty$ one has
$$\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{nlm}}(B)=\frac{1}{\|u_{nl}\|_{2}^{2}}\int_{a}^{b}|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}\,dr,$$
so the **radial density** $p_{nl}(r):=|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}/\|u_{nl}\|_{2}^{2}$ is a
probability density on $(0,\infty)$: $p_{nl}\ge0$ and
$\int_{0}^{\infty}p_{nl}(r)\,dr=1$;

(b) for $n=1,l=m=0$ one has
$$\Psi_{100}(x)=(\pi a_{\kappa}^{3})^{-1/2}e^{-r/a_{\kappa}},\qquad p_{10}(r)=4r^{2}a_{\kappa}^{-3}e^{-2r/a_{\kappa}},$$
the mean of $p_{10}$ is $\int_{0}^{\infty}r\,p_{10}(r)\,dr=3a_{\kappa}/2$, the
unique maximum of $p_{10}$ is at $r=a_{\kappa}$, the spatial density
$|\Psi_{100}|^{2}$ is strictly decreasing in $r$ and maximal at the origin,
and for every $\varepsilon>0$
$$\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{100}}\bigl(\{|x|<\varepsilon\}\bigr)=\frac{1}{6}\Bigl(\frac{2\varepsilon}{a_{\kappa}}\Bigr)^{3}+O(\varepsilon^{4})>0,$$
which tends to $0$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$: the density maximum at the
origin is not an atom of probability at any point;

(c) for every label the reduced solution has the polynomial-exponential form
$$u_{nl}(r)=c_{nl}\,r^{l+1}e^{-r/(na_{\kappa})}L_{n-l-1}^{(2l+1)}\bigl(2r/(na_{\kappa})\bigr)\qquad(c_{nl}\ne0),$$
with $L_{j}^{(a)}$ the Laguerre polynomial of integer order, so the radial
density of the level $(n,l)$ is a polynomial times $r^{2l+2}$ times a
decreasing exponential, and its normalisation constant is fixed by
$\int_{0}^{\infty}|u_{nl}|^{2}dr=\|\psi_{nlm}\|^{2}$;

(d) *Reading and scope.* The statements are conditional on P1, P2, P5, the
declared Coulomb model and the cited mathematics. The radial density is the
reading of the model's position observable on radial sets; it is not a
trajectory, an orbit or a definite distance, and the model assigns positive
probability to every open ball around the origin and to arbitrarily large
radii. No measured radius, no measured density and no identification of
$a_{\kappa}$ with a laboratory length is asserted; numerical comparison
requires the measured constants as qualified empirical inputs and is deferred.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The declared one-centre Coulomb model with $\hbar,m,\kappa>0$, $a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, $\gamma=2m\kappa/\hbar^{2}$ and bound vectors $\psi_{nlm}$, $\Psi_{nlm}$; the polar unitary and spherical harmonics of the angular-radial theory; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice.

[F1] **Bound vectors as reduced solutions.** For every $n\ge1$, $0\le l\le n-1$, $-l\le m\le l$ one has $\psi_{nlm}(x)=u_{nl}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ with $u_{nl}$ the regular solution of the radial equation at $k=\gamma/(2n)$, the functions $\psi_{nlm}$ lie in $D(H_{\kappa})$ with $H_{\kappa}\psi_{nlm}=E_{n}\psi_{nlm}$, and the normalised family $(\Psi_{nlm})$ is orthonormal ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-negative-subspace-completeness-and-degeneracy]] clauses (a), (b), [[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] clause (a)).

[F2] **Regular solutions.** The regular solution has the closed form $u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)=c\,r^{l+1}e^{-kr}L_{j}^{(2l+1)}(2kr)$ with $j=\gamma/(2k)-l-1\in\mathbb N_{0}$ and $c\ne0$, where $L_{j}^{(a)}(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{j}(-1)^{i}\binom{j+a}{j-i}x^{i}/i!$ is the $j$-th Laguerre polynomial of order $a$; it is $C^{\infty}$ on $(0,\infty)$ and square integrable exactly in this terminating case ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination]] clauses (c), (d)).

[F3] **Ground-state data.** With $a_{0}:=2/\gamma$ one has $\psi_{100}(x)=(\gamma^{3}/8\pi)^{1/2}e^{-r/a_{0}}$, $\|\psi_{100}\|=1$, $C_{\gamma}\psi_{100}=-\frac{\gamma^{2}}{4}\psi_{100}$; the radial density $p(r)=\frac{\gamma^{3}}{2}r^{2}e^{-2r/a_{0}}=4r^{2}a_{0}^{-3}e^{-2r/a_{0}}$ is a probability density with mean $3a_{0}/2$ and unique mode $a_{0}$; the spatial density is strictly decreasing in $r$ and maximal at the origin, with $\int_{|x|<\varepsilon}|\psi_{100}|^{2}dx=\frac16\bigl(\frac{2\varepsilon}{a_{0}}\bigr)^{3}+O(\varepsilon^{4})$; and $a_{0}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)=a_{\kappa}$ under $\gamma=2m\kappa/\hbar^{2}$ ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-ground-radial-probability-and-units]] clauses (a)-(e), [[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (b)).

[F4] **Polar disintegration.** For $\psi(x)=u(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ with $u$ square integrable and $Y_{lm}$ normalised in $L^{2}(S^{2},\sigma)$, and for every Borel $B$, one has $\int_{B}|\psi(x)|^{2}dx=\int_{0}^{\infty}|u(r)|^{2}\bigl(\int_{S^{2}}\mathbf 1_{B}(r\Omega)|Y_{lm}(\Omega)|^{2}d\sigma(\Omega)\bigr)dr$; this is the polar-coordinates formula for the Lebesgue integral with the surface measure $\sigma$ and Tonelli's theorem, together with $\int_{S^{2}}|Y_{lm}|^{2}d\sigma=1$ ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]).

[F5] **Position law.** In a unit vector $\psi$ the model's Born position law is $\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{B}|\psi|^{2}dx$ for every Borel $B$ ([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; insert the reduced-solution representation of the bound vectors into the spin-zero position law, disintegrate the resulting integral in polar coordinates, and transport the cited ground-state computation into the model's parametrisation.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [General radial law] Fix a label. By [F1], $\psi_{nlm}(x)=u_{nl}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ and $u_{nl}$ is a regular solution of [F2]; the unit preparation is $[\Psi_{nlm}]$ with $\Psi_{nlm}=\psi_{nlm}/\|\psi_{nlm}\|$. By [F5] its position law is $\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{nlm}}(B)=\int_{B}|\Psi_{nlm}|^{2}dx$, and since the normalisation constant is a scalar, [F4] applied to $\Psi_{nlm}$ gives the displayed formula for every Borel $B$. For a radial set $B=\{a<|x|<b\}$ the indicator $\mathbf 1_{B}(r\Omega)$ does not depend on $\Omega$ and equals $\mathbf 1_{(a,b)}(r)$, so the inner integral is $\int_{S^{2}}|Y_{lm}|^{2}d\sigma=1$ by [F4] and $\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{nlm}}(B)=\|u_{nl}\|_{2}^{-2}\int_{a}^{b}|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}dr$; the density $p_{nl}$ is nonnegative and integrates to one over $(0,\infty)$ by choosing $a=0$, $b=\infty$. This proves (a). [given, F1, F2, F4, F5, algebra]

2.1 [Ground state] Take $n=1$, $l=m=0$; then $F_{3}$ gives $\psi_{100}(x)=(\gamma^{3}/8\pi)^{1/2}e^{-r/a_{0}}$ with $\|\psi_{100}\|=1$, so $\Psi_{100}=\psi_{100}$ and the radial density of (a) is $p_{10}(r)=|u_{10}(r)|^{2}$. By [F2] with $l=j=0$ one has $u_{10}(r)=c\,r e^{-kr}L_{0}^{(1)}(2kr)$ and $L_{0}^{(1)}=1$, so $u_{10}(r)=c\,r e^{-r/a_{\kappa}}$ with $k=\gamma/2=1/a_{\kappa}$; inserting this into $|\psi_{100}|^{2}$ and polar disintegration [F4] identifies $c^{2}=4a_{\kappa}^{-3}$, that is $p_{10}(r)=4r^{2}a_{\kappa}^{-3}e^{-2r/a_{\kappa}}$. The mean, the unique mode $a_{\kappa}$, the strict decrease of the spatial density and the ball probability are the statements of [F3] rewritten with $a_{0}=a_{\kappa}$; positivity for every $\varepsilon>0$ and convergence to zero as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ follow since $(2\varepsilon/a_{\kappa})^{3}>0$ and tends to $0$. This proves (b). [step 1.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.2 [Polynomial-exponential form] For a general label, [F2] with $j=n-l-1$ and $k=\gamma/(2n)=1/(na_{\kappa})$ gives $u_{nl}(r)=c_{nl}r^{l+1}e^{-r/(na_{\kappa})}L_{n-l-1}^{(2l+1)}(2r/(na_{\kappa}))$ with $c_{nl}\ne0$; the normalisation $\int_{0}^{\infty}|u_{nl}|^{2}dr=\|\psi_{nlm}\|^{2}$ is the case $a=0$, $b=\infty$ of step 1.1. This is (c). [step 1.1, F1, F2]

3.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 gives (a), step 2.1 gives (b) and step 2.2 gives (c); only the declared model, P1, P2, P5 and the cited mathematics were used, so the reading is conditional as recorded in (d), no orbit, trajectory, measured radius or empirical identification is asserted, and the model assigns positive probability to every ball around the origin and to arbitrarily large radii. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **The radial density is not a radial observable.** The quantity $p_{nl}$ is
  the disintegration of the position law on radial Borel sets, a reading of
  the declared position observable; the model does not assign the radius as an
  independent sharp observable, and no commutation or measurement claim about
  a radius operator is made.
- **Scales.** The two length scales $a_{\kappa}$ and the energy scale
  $\hbar^{2}/(2ma_{\kappa}^{2})$ are model data fixed by $\hbar,m,\kappa$; the
  identification of $a_{\kappa}$ with a physical Bohr radius of a hydrogen
  atom is the tested identification of
  [[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (e) and
  carries its uncertainty.

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 8.1.2, printed pages 187-190 (the radial eigenfunctions u_n^l, the ground-state radial function, the r-expectation values and the probability outside classically allowed radii)

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 10.4, printed pages 229-235 (the explicit normalised bound states and the lowest eigenvalue, with the ground-state formula)

The scales a_kappa and the density are model data; the item asserts no measured radius, no orbit, no trajectory, no formation or decay process, and does not identify a_kappa with any measured length.

items.title: The declared two-body Coulomb model: reduced-mass decomposition, relative levels as thresholds and the absence of stationary total states
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the framework postulates P1, P2, P4 and P5 and the readings of the
declared two-body Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a), (b),
(d) and (e) with declared masses $m_{1},m_{2}>0$, charge parameter $q>0$,
coupling $\kappa=q^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$, reduced mass
$\mu=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$, the centre-of-mass/relative coordinate map
$\Phi$, its unitary $U_{\Phi}$, the total operator $H_{2}$ on
$H^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$, the centre-of-mass kinetic operator $T_{R}$
and the relative operator $C_{\mu}$, together with the one-centre results
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] applied with mass
parameter $\mu$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the identity $U_{\Phi}H_{2}U_{\Phi}^{-1}=T_{R}\otimes I+I\otimes C_{\mu}$
holds on the tensor product, and $C_{\mu}$ is exactly the one-centre Coulomb
operator of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (b) with mass
parameter $\mu$; the model's relative problem is therefore the declared
one-centre Coulomb model with parameters $(\hbar,\mu,\kappa)$;

(b) the relative bound energies are
$$\mathcal E_{n}:=-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\mu a_{\mu}^{2}n^{2}},\qquad a_{\mu}:=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{\mu\kappa}\qquad(n\ge1),$$
with model degeneracy $n^{2}$ within the relative problem and the same radial
and position readings as in
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-state-radial-distributions]] with $m$
replaced by $\mu$;

(c) the total operator $H_{2}$ has no eigenvalues at all:
$\sigma(H_{2})=[-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}},+\infty)$, the whole negative
part $[-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}},0)$ of the spectrum is continuous,
and each relative bound energy $\mathcal E_{n}$ is a threshold of the
continuous spectrum of $H_{2}$ rather than an eigenvalue;

(d) if $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R};\mathbb C)$ and $u$ is a relative
bound vector with $C_{\mu}u=\mathcal E_{n}u$, then the product vector
$\varphi\otimes u$ is an eigenvector of $H_{2}$ only if $\varphi=0$; the total
momentum operators $P_{R,j}$ are self-adjoint with no nonzero eigenvectors in
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R};\mathbb C)$, so the model possesses no normalisable
state of definite total momentum, and by the stationary-state criterion no
product of a centre-of-mass state with a relative bound state is a stationary
state of the two-body system;

(e) *Reading.* The reduced mass obeys $\mu=\frac{m_{1}}{1+m_{1}/m_{2}}$ and
satisfies $\mu\le\min\{m_{1},m_{2}\}$ with $\mu\to m_{1}$ as $m_{2}\to\infty$
at fixed $m_{1}$; the model reads the one-centre model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (b) with mass
$m_{1}$ as the fixed-nucleus limiting description, and the relative energies
$\mathcal E_{n}$ are strictly weaker in magnitude than the fixed-nucleus
energies $-\frac{m_{1}\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$;

(f) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared
two-body model and the cited mathematics; it asserts no measured mass, charge
or level, no transition, photon or radiation statement, no binding or
formation dynamics, and no identification of the model with a laboratory
atom beyond the tested identification of clause (e) of the model definition.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The declared two-body Coulomb model with $m_{1},m_{2},\hbar>0$, coupling $\kappa>0$, reduced mass $\mu=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$, the coordinate map $\Phi$, the unitary $U_{\Phi}$, the operators $T_{R}$, $C_{\mu}$ and $H_{2}$; the one-centre results with mass parameter $\mu$; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice.

[F1] **Model data.** $C_{\mu}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\mu}\Delta_{r}-\frac{\kappa}{|r|}$ on $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{r};\mathbb C)=D(C_{\mu})$ is exactly the one-centre Coulomb operator of [[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (b) with mass parameter $\mu$; $H_{2}$ with $D(H_{2})=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$ is self-adjoint, and $\Phi(x_{1},x_{2})=(R,r)$ is the centre-of-mass/relative coordinate map of clause (d) of the same definition ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]]).

[F2] **Two-body decomposition and its spectrum.** $\Phi$ is a linear isomorphism with $|\det\Phi|=1$, $U_{\Phi}$ is unitary, $U_{\Phi}H_{2}U_{\Phi}^{-1}=T_{R}\otimes I+I\otimes C_{\mu}$ under the identification $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6})\cong L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R})\widehat\otimes L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{r})$, and $\sigma(H_{2})=[-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}},\infty)$ with no eigenvalues at all: the negative part $[-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}},0)$ consists entirely of continuous spectrum, each relative bound energy $-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$ is a threshold of the continuous spectrum rather than an eigenvalue, and in particular a relative bound state tensored with any centre-of-mass state is not an eigenvector of $H_{2}$ ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]] clauses (a), (c), (d), [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]).

[F3] **Total momentum.** The operators $P_{R,j}=\frac{\hbar}{i}\partial_{R_{j}}$ on their maximal domains are self-adjoint and have no nonzero eigenvectors in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R};\mathbb C)$; consequently every eigenvector equation for $H_{2}$ is incompatible with a normalisable state of definite total momentum ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]] clause (e)).

[F4] **One-centre results with mass $\mu$.** The one-centre Coulomb model with parameters $(\hbar,\mu,\kappa)$ has bound energies $\mathcal E_{n}=-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$, $n\ge1$, the eigenspace at $\mathcal E_{n}$ having dimension $n^{2}$ and consisting of the transported Laguerre solutions, with the radial and position readings of the one-centre items ([[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] clauses (a), (b), [[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-state-radial-distributions]] clauses (a), (c)).

[F5] **Stationary states.** For an assigned energy observable, a nonzero vector is an eigenvector if and only if its pure preparation is stationary ([[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] clause (c), [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; read the centre-of-mass/relative decomposition and the spectral theorem's two-body clauses in the model, identify the relative operator with the one-centre Coulomb operator of mass $\mu$, and compute the reduced-mass factor.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Decomposition and relative problem] By [F1] and [F2], $U_{\Phi}H_{2}U_{\Phi}^{-1}=T_{R}\otimes I+I\otimes C_{\mu}$ and $C_{\mu}$ is the one-centre Coulomb operator with mass parameter $\mu$; with the one-centre model definition this is (a). Applying [F4] with mass parameter $\mu$ gives the relative bound energies $\mathcal E_{n}=-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\mu a_{\mu}^{2}n^{2}}$ with $a_{\mu}=\hbar^{2}/(\mu\kappa)$, degeneracy $n^{2}$ and the stated radial and position readings; this is (b). [given, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Total spectrum and product vectors] By [F2] the total operator $H_{2}$ has no eigenvalues, $\sigma(H_{2})=[-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}},\infty)$ and the negative part of the spectrum is continuous, each $\mathcal E_{n}$ being a threshold and not an eigenvalue; this is (c). If $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R})$ and $C_{\mu}u=\mathcal E_{n}u$ with $u\ne0$, then by the decomposition of step 1.1, $\bigl(T_{R}\otimes I+I\otimes C_{\mu}\bigr)(\varphi\otimes u)=(T_{R}\varphi)\otimes u+\mathcal E_{n}(\varphi\otimes u)$; this equals $\lambda(\varphi\otimes u)$ for some $\lambda$ if and only if $T_{R}\varphi=(\lambda-\mathcal E_{n})\varphi$, and by [F3] the operator $T_{R}$ has no nonzero eigenvectors in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R})$, so $\varphi=0$; moreover by [F3] no nonzero vector in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R})$ is an eigenvector of any $P_{R,j}$, so the model has no normalisable state of definite total momentum. By [F5], an eigenvector equation for $H_{2}$ is necessary and sufficient for a stationary pure preparation, so no product of a centre-of-mass state with a relative bound state is stationary. This is (d). [step 1.1, F2, F3, F5, algebra]

2.2 [Reduced-mass factor] By algebra, $\mu=\frac{m_{1}m_{2}}{m_{1}+m_{2}}=\frac{m_{1}}{1+m_{1}/m_{2}}$, hence $\mu<m_{1}$ and $\mu<m_{2}$, so $\mu\le\min\{m_{1},m_{2}\}$; for fixed $m_{1}$ the expression $\frac{m_{1}}{1+m_{1}/m_{2}}$ tends to $m_{1}$ as $m_{2}\to\infty$. Comparing the relative energies $\mathcal E_{n}=-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$ with the fixed-nucleus energies $-\frac{m_{1}\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$ of the one-centre model with mass $m_{1}$, the relative binding magnitudes are smaller by the factor $\mu/m_{1}=1/(1+m_{1}/m_{2})<1$, which is the reduced-mass correction of the model; this is (e). [step 1.1, F1, algebra]

3.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 gives (a) and (b), step 2.1 gives (c) and (d) and step 2.2 gives (e); only the declared two-body model, P1, P2, P4, P5 and the cited mathematics were used, so the statement is conditional as recorded in (f) and asserts no empirical identification, measured parameter, transition, photon or formation dynamics. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why the relative levels are not total energies.** The centre-of-mass
  motion of an isolated two-body system is free in this model, so its operator
  has purely continuous spectrum; a relative bound state is an internal state
  and cannot be a stationary state of the total system. Any statement that a
  hydrogen atom "is" an eigenstate of a two-body Hamiltonian conflicts with
  this decomposition and is not made.
- **Threshold reading.** The bottom of the continuous spectrum,
  $\mathcal E_{1}=-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}$, coincides with the
  relative ground energy; the model reads it as the continuum threshold of the
  relative problem, and no ionisation or scattering process is described here.

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 10.1-10.2, printed pages 221-225 (the one-particle reduction of the two-body Coulomb problem and the parameters of the relative equation)
D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 4.3, printed pages 111-112 (the hydrogen atom as a two-body Coulomb problem with the electron mass in the relative equation)

items.statement:
## Remarks

- **What the page establishes.** The pair declares a central-potential model
  ([[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]) and a Coulomb and
  two-body hydrogen model
  ([[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]]), proves the
  spherical reduction of smooth compactly supported states
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-spherical-reduction-of-smooth-states]]), and derives
  the energy-observable and flow reading
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]]), the bound
  energies $E_{n}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$ with $n^{2}$-fold
  model degeneracy and the completeness of the bound states in the negative
  spectral subspace with a nonzero continuum
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]]), the radial
  and ground-state position readings
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-state-radial-distributions]]), and the
  two-body reduced-mass decomposition with the relative levels as thresholds
  and the absence of stationary total states
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-two-body-reduced-threshold-and-total-momentum]]). Every
  item is conditional on the cited postulates, the declared model and the
  cited mathematics; none establishes that the model or its postulates
  describes nature.

- **What the page does not contain.** No experiment, no reported spectral
  line, no count, no calibration, no detector model, no sampling assumption
  and no statistical inference appears on the page, and no numerical value of
  $\hbar$, $m$, $\kappa$, $q$, $m_{1}$, $m_{2}$ or $\varepsilon_{0}$ is fixed
  by any item. The transition frequencies, line intensities and selection
  rules of a hydrogen-like system require the radiation extension and the
  light-matter coupling of later items, and the scattering, ionisation and
  continuum processes require the three-dimensional scattering pair; neither
  is built or assumed here. The dipole matrix elements and their angular
  selection rules are reserved to the light-matter pair, and the numerical
  comparison with measured spectra to a future experiment item with its own
  preparation, calibration, sampling and uncertainty record; no such item
  exists in this batch.

- **Excluded physics.** The gross-structure model excludes spin and magnetic
  couplings, relativistic fine structure and the splitting of the
  $n^{2}$-fold degeneracy, finite nuclear size and nuclear structure,
  recoil corrections beyond the two-body reduced-mass formulation, QED
  corrections including the Lamb shift, hyperfine structure, shielding and
  many-body modifications of the $1/r$ potential, external fields, and
  radiation reaction. The source treatments describe several of these
  corrections as small compared with the gross-structure energies; no such
  magnitude comparison is a premise of any item on this page, and none of the
  excluded effects is claimed to be negligible by this page.

- **Empirical status of the model's numbers.** Statements such as "the
  hydrogen ground-state binding energy is about $13.6$ electronvolts" are
  conditional evaluations of the model's formula with measured constants
  (such as the fine-structure constant, the electron-to-proton mass ratio or
  the Rydberg constant) as inputs; they carry the uncertainties, conditions
  and conventions of those inputs and are not measurements of hydrogen by
  this page. Agreement of a computed transition frequency with a measured
  line would test the combined model, apparatus and constant assumptions; it
  would not be a deductive proof of the model.

- **Physical-interface note.** The model declarations, the readings and the
  scope exclusions above are the public physical interface of the pair;
  changing them requires the ordinary direct and indirect consumer review
  under the workflow rules, and the empirical qualifications carried here
  must be preserved by every later item that consumes these results.

items.title: Bound-energy parametrisations of the Coulomb model: exact identities, units and the reduced-mass factor
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the declared one-centre Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with
parameters $\hbar>0$, $m>0$, coupling $\kappa>0$ and length scale
$a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, the bound-energy result
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] and the two-body
reading [[pthm-nrqm-central-two-body-reduced-threshold-and-total-momentum]]
with masses $m_{1},m_{2}>0$ and reduced mass
$\mu=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$. Let the charge parameter be $q>0$ with
$\kappa=q^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$, let $c$ be the speed of light of the SI
conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (c), and put
$$\alpha:=\frac{q^{2}}{4\pi\varepsilon_{0}\hbar c}=\frac{\kappa}{\hbar c},$$
the dimensionless coupling of the model. Then the following identities hold
exactly for the declared parameters:

(a) $E_{n}:=-\dfrac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}=-\dfrac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}n^{2}}$
for every $n\ge1$, so
$\dfrac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}=\dfrac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}}$ and
$E_{1}=-\dfrac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}}$;

(b) $\kappa=\alpha\hbar c$, hence
$E_{n}=-\dfrac{m\alpha^{2}c^{2}}{2n^{2}}$ and
$a_{\kappa}=\dfrac{\hbar}{m\alpha c}$;

(c) the relative bound energies of the two-body model are
$\mathcal E_{n}=-\dfrac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}
=\dfrac{\mu}{m_{1}}\Bigl(-\dfrac{m_{1}\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}\Bigr)$
with
$\dfrac{\mu}{m_{1}}=\dfrac{1}{1+m_{1}/m_{2}}\in(0,1)$;

(d) in the reference units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (b), $[\hbar]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-1}}$,
$[\kappa]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{3}\,s^{-2}}$,
$[a_{\kappa}]=\mathrm m$,
$[E_{n}]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-2}}=\mathrm J$ and $[\alpha]=1$, so every
displayed identity is dimensionally consistent;

(e) the bottom of the continuous spectrum of the total two-body operator is
$\mathcal E_{1}=-\dfrac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}$, which coincides with the
relative ground energy, and the total operator has no eigenvalue there.

The identities are conditional model computations in terms of declared
parameters; no numerical value of any parameter is assigned, and no measured
quantity is reported. A numerical evaluation of $E_{1}$ requires measured
values of constants such as $\alpha$ and of the mass ratio $m_{1}/m_{2}$ as
qualified empirical premises; it is not performed here.

## Verification

**Given:** The declared Coulomb and two-body model with $\hbar,m,m_{1},m_{2},\kappa,q,\varepsilon_{0},c>0$; $\alpha=\kappa/(\hbar c)$; $a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$; $\mu=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$; the bound-energy and two-body results of the cited items.

[L1] **One-centre bound energies.** The eigenvalues of $H_{\kappa}$ are exactly $E_{n}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}n^{2}}$, $n\ge1$ ([[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] clauses (a), (b), [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-ground-radial-probability-and-units]] clause (e)).

[L2] **Two-body energies and threshold.** The relative bound energies are $\mathcal E_{n}=-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$, the reduced mass is $\mu=\frac{m_{1}m_{2}}{m_{1}+m_{2}}=\frac{m_{1}}{1+m_{1}/m_{2}}$, and the bottom of the continuous spectrum of the total operator is $-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}$, each $\mathcal E_{n}$ being a threshold and not an eigenvalue ([[pthm-nrqm-central-two-body-reduced-threshold-and-total-momentum]] clauses (b), (c), (e), [[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (d)).

[L3] **Units and conventions.** The reference units are m, s, kg, C; the dimension map assigns $[\hbar]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-1}}$, energy $[\cdot]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-2}}$, length $[\cdot]=\mathrm m$ and charge $[q]=\mathrm C$, with $c$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $\varepsilon_{0}=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$, so $[\kappa]=[\frac{q^{2}}{\varepsilon_{0}}]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{3}\,s^{-2}}$ and $[\alpha]=1$; numerical values of the measured constants are not fixed ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clauses (b), (c), (d)).

**Proof technique:** direct; substitute the definitions of $a_{\kappa}$, $\alpha$ and $\mu$ into the model's bound-energy formulae and check the units by the dimension map.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [L1]-[L3].

1.1 [Length-scale identity] By definition $a_{\kappa}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{m\kappa}$, so $a_{\kappa}^{2}=\frac{\hbar^{4}}{m^{2}\kappa^{2}}$ and $\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\cdot\frac{m^{2}\kappa^{2}}{\hbar^{4}}=\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}$; multiplying by $n^{-2}$ gives the equality of the two expressions for $E_{n}$ in (a), and $n=1$ gives $E_{1}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}}$. [given, L1, algebra]

1.2 [Fine-structure parametrisation] By definition $\alpha=\frac{\kappa}{\hbar c}$, hence $\kappa=\alpha\hbar c$ and $\kappa^{2}=\alpha^{2}\hbar^{2}c^{2}$; substituting into $E_{n}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$ gives $E_{n}=-\frac{m\alpha^{2}c^{2}}{2n^{2}}$, and substituting into $a_{\kappa}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{m\kappa}$ gives $a_{\kappa}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{m\alpha\hbar c}=\frac{\hbar}{m\alpha c}$; this is (b). [given, L1, algebra]

1.3 [Reduced-mass factor] By [L2], $\mathcal E_{n}=-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$ and $\mu=\frac{m_{1}}{1+m_{1}/m_{2}}$, so $\mu=\frac{\mu}{m_{1}}\cdot m_{1}$ gives $\mathcal E_{n}=\frac{\mu}{m_{1}}\bigl(-\frac{m_{1}\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}\bigr)$, where the bracket is the fixed-nucleus energy of the one-centre model with mass parameter $m_{1}$; since $m_{1},m_{2}>0$ one has $0<\frac{1}{1+m_{1}/m_{2}}<1$, so the relative binding magnitudes are strictly smaller than the fixed-nucleus ones. This is (c). [given, L1, L2, algebra]

1.4 [Dimensions] Using [L3]: $[a_{\kappa}]=\frac{[\hbar]^{2}}{[m][\kappa]}=\frac{(\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-1}})^{2}}{\mathrm{kg}\cdot\mathrm{kg\,m^{3}\,s^{-2}}}=\mathrm m$; $[\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{\hbar^{2}}]=\frac{\mathrm{kg}\cdot(\mathrm{kg\,m^{3}\,s^{-2}})^{2}}{(\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-1}})^{2}}=\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-2}}=\mathrm J$; $[\frac{\hbar}{m\alpha c}]=\frac{\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-1}}}{\mathrm{kg}\cdot 1\cdot\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}}=\mathrm m$; and $[\alpha]=\frac{[\kappa]}{[\hbar][c]}=\frac{\mathrm{kg\,m^{3}\,s^{-2}}}{\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-1}}\cdot\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}}=1$. Hence the identities of (a) and (b) are dimensionally consistent, which is (d). [given, L3, algebra]

2.1 [Threshold and assembly] By [L2] the bottom of the continuous spectrum of the total operator is $-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}=\mathcal E_{1}$, and the relative ground energy is a threshold and not an eigenvalue of the total operator, which is (e). Steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 give (a)-(d); no numerical value of any parameter was used, so the example is conditional as recorded. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, L2] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why no numbers appear.** Evaluating $E_{1}$ in electronvolts would
  require measured inputs such as the fine-structure constant and the
  electron-to-proton mass ratio; the model's own parameters are not measured
  by this page, and the empirical premises, their uncertainties and the
  comparison with observed spectra belong to a dedicated experiment item,
  which does not yet exist.
- **Fixed-nucleus reference.** The bracket in (c) is the fixed-nucleus energy
  of the one-centre model with mass parameter $m_{1}$; it is a reference
  quantity of the declared limiting reading and not a measured quantity, and
  the limit $m_{2}\to\infty$ is a declared reading, not an operator
  convergence theorem.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 8.1, printed pages 184-186 (equations (8.25)-(8.27): E = -Z^2 mu e^4/(2 n^2 (4 pi eps_0 hbar)^2), the Rydberg constant R = (1/2) mu (e^2/(4 pi eps_0 hbar))^2 and E = -R/n^2)

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 4.3.1, printed pages 114-116 (equations (4.30) and (4.31): the energy spectrum and the Bohr radius, and the fine-structure-constant rewriting E = -alpha^2 m_e c^2/(2n^2))

items.title: Low-lying radial distributions of the Coulomb model: normalisations, moments and the failure of cross-l orthogonality of reduced functions
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the declared one-centre Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with
parameters $\hbar>0$, $m>0$, coupling $\kappa>0$ and
$a:=a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, and the radial reading of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-state-radial-distributions]]. In the
notation of that item, $u_{nl}$ denotes the reduced regular solution with
$\psi_{nlm}(x)=u_{nl}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ and $p_{nl}=|u_{nl}|^{2}/\|u_{nl}\|_{2}^{2}$
the radial density of the normalised bound state. Then:

(a) $u_{10}(r)=2a^{-3/2}r\,e^{-r/a}$ and
$u_{20}(r)=2^{-3/2}a^{-3/2}\bigl(2r-\frac{r^{2}}{a}\bigr)e^{-r/(2a)}$ and
$u_{21}(r)=2^{-3/2}3^{-1/2}a^{-5/2}r^{2}e^{-r/(2a)}$;

(b) $\|u_{10}\|_{2}=\|u_{20}\|_{2}=\|u_{21}\|_{2}=1$, so for these states the
reduced solution is already normalised and $p_{nl}=|u_{nl}|^{2}$;

(c) the moments
$$\int_{0}^{\infty}r\,p_{10}(r)\,dr=\frac{3a}{2},\qquad \int_{0}^{\infty}r^{2}p_{10}(r)\,dr=3a^{2},\qquad \int_{0}^{\infty}r\,p_{20}(r)\,dr=6a,\qquad \int_{0}^{\infty}r\,p_{21}(r)\,dr=5a,$$
and
$$\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{p_{20}(r)}{r}\,dr=\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{p_{21}(r)}{r}\,dr=\frac{1}{4a};$$

(d) the same-$l$ pair is orthogonal,
$\int_{0}^{\infty}u_{10}(r)u_{20}(r)\,dr=0$, while the different-$l$ pair is
not: $\int_{0}^{\infty}u_{20}(r)u_{21}(r)\,dr=-\frac{\sqrt 3}{2}\ne0$, so the
reduced radial functions of different angular momentum are not orthogonal in
$L^{2}((0,\infty),dr)$, the orthogonality of the full bound states being
carried by the angular factor;

(e) the closed forms of (a) agree with the standard radial functions
$R_{nl}=u_{nl}/r$ of the cited treatments for these states, and the value
$\int r\,p_{nl}$ for the circular state $n=2$, $l=1$ agrees with the general
circular-orbit formula $\langle r\rangle_{n,n-1}=n(n+\tfrac12)a$ at $n=2$;

(f) *Scope.* The computation is conditional on the declared model and the
cited mathematics; $a$ is a model scale, the moments are moments of the
model's radial reading and not measured radii, and no measurement, orbit or
trajectory is asserted.

## Verification

**Given:** The declared one-centre Coulomb model with $\hbar,m,\kappa>0$, $a=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, $\gamma=2/a$; the reduced solutions $u_{nl}$ of the model with $\psi_{nlm}=u_{nl}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$; the Axiom of Countable Choice.

[L1] **Exponential moments.** For every $\lambda>0$ and integer $k\ge0$, $\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{k}e^{-\lambda r}dr=k!/\lambda^{k+1}$ ([[lem-nrqm-central-exponential-moments]]).

[L2] **Reduced solutions.** $u_{nl}(r)=c_{nl}r^{l+1}e^{-r/(na)}L_{n-l-1}^{(2l+1)}(2r/(na))$ with $c_{nl}\ne0$ and $L_{j}^{(a)}$ the Laguerre polynomial $L_{j}^{(a)}(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{j}(-1)^{i}\binom{j+a}{j-i}x^{i}/i!$; for $j=0$ one has $L_{0}^{(a)}=1$ and for $j=1$ one has $L_{1}^{(a)}(x)=1+a-x$ ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination]] clause (d), [[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-state-radial-distributions]] clause (c)).

[L3] **Radial reading.** For a radial set the position law of the normalised bound state is $\int_{a}^{b}p_{nl}(r)dr$ with $p_{nl}=|u_{nl}|^{2}/\|u_{nl}\|_{2}^{2}$, and $\int_{0}^{\infty}p_{nl}dr=1$ ([[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-state-radial-distributions]] clause (a), [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b)).

**Proof technique:** direct; insert the Laguerre data into the closed forms, evaluate the resulting elementary integrals with the exponential-moments lemma, and compare with the cited radial functions.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [L1]-[L3].

1.1 [Closed forms] For $n=1$, $l=0$: $j=0$, $k=1/(na)=1/a$, so [L2] gives $u_{10}(r)=c\,r e^{-r/a}$. For $n=2$, $l=0$: $j=1$, $L_{1}^{(1)}(x)=2-x$ and $k=1/(2a)$, so $u_{20}(r)=c\,r e^{-r/(2a)}(2-r/a)$. For $n=2$, $l=1$: $j=0$, $L_{0}^{(3)}=1$ and $k=1/(2a)$, so $u_{21}(r)=c\,r^{2}e^{-r/(2a)}$. The constants $c$ are fixed by the normalisation condition $\|u_{nl}\|_{2}=1$, evaluated in the next step, giving the displayed coefficients of (a). [given, L2, algebra]

2.1 [Normalisations] By [L1] with $\lambda=2/a$: $\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{2}e^{-2r/a}dr=2/(2/a)^{3}=a^{3}/4$ and $\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{4}e^{-2r/a}dr=24/(2/a)^{5}=3a^{5}/4$; hence $\int_{0}^{\infty}(2a^{-3/2}r e^{-r/a})^{2}dr=4a^{-3}\cdot a^{3}/4=1$, so $c=2a^{-3/2}$ for $u_{10}$ and $\|u_{10}\|_{2}=1$. By [L1] with $\lambda=1/a$: $\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{2}e^{-r/a}dr=2a^{3}$, $\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{3}e^{-r/a}dr=6a^{4}$, $\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{4}e^{-r/a}dr=24a^{5}$; expanding $(2-r/a)^{2}=4-4r/a+r^{2}/a^{2}$ gives $\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{2}(2-r/a)^{2}e^{-r/a}dr=8a^{3}-24a^{3}+24a^{3}=8a^{3}$, so $c=2^{-3/2}a^{-3/2}$ yields $\|u_{20}\|_{2}=1$; and $c^{2}\int r^{4}e^{-r/a}dr=c^{2}\cdot 24a^{5}=1$ gives $c=24^{-1/2}a^{-5/2}=2^{-3/2}3^{-1/2}a^{-5/2}$ for $u_{21}$. This is (b). [step 1.1, L1, algebra]

2.2 [Moments of the ground state] With $p_{10}=4a^{-3}r^{2}e^{-2r/a}$, [L1] gives $\int r\,p_{10}=4a^{-3}\cdot 2!/(2/a)^{3}=4a^{-3}\cdot 2a^{3}/8=3a/2$, and $\int r^{2}p_{10}=4a^{-3}\cdot 3!/(2/a)^{4}=4a^{-3}\cdot 6a^{4}/16=3a^{2}$; the first is the mean of the ground radial density, and $3a^{2}-(3a/2)^{2}=3a^{2}/4$ its variance. [step 1.1, L1, algebra]

2.3 [Moments of the $n=2$ states] With $p_{20}=2^{-3}a^{-3}r^{2}(2-r/a)^{2}e^{-r/a}$ and $p_{21}=24^{-1}a^{-5}r^{4}e^{-r/a}$, [L1] gives $\int r\,p_{20}=2^{-3}a^{-3}\int r^{3}(2-r/a)^{2}e^{-r/a}dr=2^{-3}a^{-3}\cdot a^{4}\int x^{3}(4-4x+x^{2})e^{-x}dx=2^{-3}a^{-3}\cdot a^{4}(4\cdot 3!-4\cdot 4!+5!)=2^{-3}a^{-3}\cdot 48a^{4}=6a$; and $\int r\,p_{21}=24^{-1}a^{-5}\cdot 5!a^{6}=5a$. Moreover $\int r^{-1}p_{20}=2^{-3}a^{-3}\int r(2-r/a)^{2}e^{-r/a}dr=2^{-3}a^{-3}(4\cdot 1!\,a^{2}-4\cdot 2!\,a^{2}+3!\,a^{2})=2^{-3}a^{-3}\cdot 2a^{2}=a^{-1}/4$, and $\int r^{-1}p_{21}=24^{-1}a^{-5}\cdot 3!a^{4}=a^{-1}/4$. This is (c). [step 1.1, L1, algebra]

2.4 [Overlaps] With $u_{10}=2a^{-3/2}re^{-r/a}$ and $u_{20}=2^{-3/2}a^{-3/2}(2r-r^{2}/a)e^{-r/(2a)}$ one has $\int u_{10}u_{20}dr=2^{-1/2}a^{-3}\int(2r^{2}-r^{3}/a)e^{-3r/(2a)}dr$; by [L1] with $\lambda=3/(2a)$, $\int r^{2}e^{-3r/(2a)}dr=2(2a/3)^{3}=16a^{3}/27$ and $\int r^{3}e^{-3r/(2a)}dr=6(2a/3)^{4}=32a^{4}/27$, so the bracket is $2\cdot 16a^{3}/27-(32a^{4}/27)/a=0$: the same-$l$ pair is orthogonal. With $u_{21}=2^{-3/2}3^{-1/2}a^{-5/2}r^{2}e^{-r/(2a)}$, the cross overlap is $\int u_{20}u_{21}dr=2^{-3}3^{-1/2}a^{-4}\int(2r^{3}-r^{4}/a)e^{-r/a}dr=2^{-3}3^{-1/2}a^{-4}(2\cdot 6a^{4}-24a^{4})=2^{-3}3^{-1/2}(-12)=-3/(2\sqrt3)=-\sqrt3/2$, nonzero. This is (d). [step 1.1, L1, algebra]

3.1 [Cross-checks and scope] Since $R_{nl}=u_{nl}/r$, step 1.1 gives $R_{10}=2a^{-3/2}e^{-r/a}$, $R_{20}=2^{-3/2}a^{-3/2}(2-r/a)e^{-r/(2a)}$ and $R_{21}=2^{-3/2}3^{-1/2}a^{-3/2}(r/a)e^{-r/(2a)}$, which agree with the cited tabulated radial functions, and the value $5a$ of step 2.3 agrees with the circular-orbit formula $\langle r\rangle_{n,n-1}=n(n+\tfrac12)a$ at $n=2$; this is (e). Only the declared model, the cited mathematics and the exponential-moments lemma were used, and $a$ remains a model scale, so the scope statement (f) holds. [step 1.1, step 2.3, L1, L2, L3] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why cross-$l$ overlaps need not vanish.** The full bound states
  $\psi_{nlm}$ and $\psi_{n'l'm'}$ are orthogonal in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$
  whenever the angular factors $Y_{lm},Y_{l'm'}$ are orthogonal, even if the
  reduced radial functions overlap; the nonzero value $-\sqrt3/2$ computed in
  (d) is exactly such a case. No orthogonality of reduced functions across
  angular momenta is claimed anywhere on this pair.
- **Moments are readings, not measurements.** The mean radius and the inverse
  radius are moments of the model's radial reading; the inverse-radius value
  $1/(4a)$ for the two $n=2$ states is a consistency check with the model's
  virial-type relation and is not compared with any measured quantity here.

items.title: Empirical status of the hydrogen spectrum on this pair: pending spectroscopy evidence and the limits of the model's spectral statements
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **What the pair's spectral statements are.** The model's content is the
  conditional spectral statement of
  [[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]]: bound energies
  $E_{n}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$ with $n^{2}$-fold model
  degeneracy, a complete negative spectral subspace and a nonzero continuum,
  together with the two-body threshold reading of
  [[pthm-nrqm-central-two-body-reduced-threshold-and-total-momentum]]. These
  are statements about the declared model and its assigned parameters; they
  are not statements about any measured hydrogen line.

- **Why no experiment appears on this pair.** The design reservation for this
  pair names a spectroscopy data candidate and marks it pending. No
  source-backed observation record with preparation, apparatus, calibration,
  sampling and uncertainty was harvested for this batch, so no experiment
  item is built and no measured wavelength, frequency or transition is
  reported. The source treatments do describe the Lyman, Balmer, Paschen and
  Brackett series and the historical Balmer fit; this page neither reproduces
  their numerical values nor treats them as its own observations, and the
  comparison of the model with measured spectra is deferred to a future
  experiment item carrying its own uncertainty record.

- **What a comparison would presuppose.** A transition-frequency statement
  $\nu=(E_{n}-E_{n'})/h$ is a reading of the model together with the radiation
  extension and the light-matter coupling of later pairs; it is not made on
  this page. Any comparison with a measured line would test the combined
  model, apparatus and constant assumptions: the preparation and isolation
  idealization, the identification of the species parameters with measured
  masses and charges, the treatment of linewidth, Doppler and instrumental
  response, and the sampling model of the recorded sample. Agreement of a
  finite set of measured lines with the predicted values would be evidence
  about the combined assumptions; it would not be a deductive proof of the
  model, and disagreement would require the same auxiliary assumptions to be
  examined before the model is rejected.

- **Excluded corrections and their status.** The gross-structure model omits
  spin, relativistic fine structure, finite nuclear size, QED corrections
  including the Lamb shift, hyperfine structure and shielding, as recorded in
  [[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (f); the
  source treatments describe some of these corrections and their
  consequences, but no magnitude, splitting or numerical value is asserted or
  used by this pair.

- **Identification caution.** The assignment of the model's parameters to a
  laboratory hydrogen atom is the tested identification of clause (e) of the
  model definition under the preparation and apparatus postulate
  ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]); it is not derived from
  the mathematics of the model and carries the uncertainty of that
  identification. The model's spectral statements remain conditional until
  such an identification, with its qualifications, is supplied.

items.title: Scope of the central-potential and hydrogen examples page
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **What the page contains.** Two conditional computations and one status
  record in the declared Coulomb model: the exact equivalence of the
  bound-energy parametrisations in terms of $(m,\kappa)$, $(\hbar,m,a_{\kappa})$
  and $(m,\alpha,c)$, the reduced-mass factor between the relative and
  fixed-nucleus energies, and the dimensional checks of those identities
  ([[ex-nrqm-central-hydrogen-bound-energy-units-and-reduced-mass]]); the
  explicit reduced radial functions, normalisations and low moments for the
  states with $n\le2$, including the check that reduced radial functions of
  different angular momentum are not orthogonal
  ([[ex-nrqm-central-hydrogen-radial-distributions-and-moments]]); and the
  empirical-status record deferring the comparison with measured spectra
  ([[rem-nrqm-central-hydrogen-spectroscopy-status]]).

- **What the page does not contain.** No experiment, no reported line, no
  wavelength or frequency value, no count, no calibration and no statistical
  inference appears; no item assigns a numerical value to any model parameter
  or measured constant, and none of the computations establishes that the
  model or its postulates describes nature. The identification of a concrete
  hydrogen atom with the declared model is a tested identification under the
  preparation and apparatus postulate
  ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) and is not made here.

- **Dependence on the A page.** Every statement of the page is conditional on
  the declared Coulomb model, its assigned energy observable and the spectral
  theorem
  ([[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]],
  [[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]]); the model
  scales $a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$ and the energies are model data, not
  measured lengths or energies.

- **Deferred content.** Transition frequencies, line intensities, selection
  rules and photon statements belong to the radiation and light-matter items
  of the quantum-mechanics track; scattering and ionisation belong to the
  three-dimensional scattering pair. The numerical spectroscopic comparison
  remains a pending experiment candidate and is not anticipated by any claim
  of this page.
